newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate fends off weak peso to end flat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate fends off weak peso to end flat.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate recovered from earlier increases to close its first session of the year on Thursday unchanged at 25.25 percent as the market awaited inflation data, traders said.
"A weak peso and a slump in the bourse hit us early on," a trader said. "Nonetheless, trading volume was thin and for now dealers prefer to sit out and wait for December inflation figures."
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.4 of a peso weaker, at 7.8940/7.8990. The overnight Cetes rate reached a high of 25.75 percent during the session.
Dealers put peso weakness down to increases in yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, up to 6.74 percent compared to 6.64 percent in late trade on Tuesday.
Bank overnight rates closed up 55 basis points at 26.30 percent, after zigzagging between 25.50 and 26.50 percent.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortfalls by auctioning one overnight credit for 2.471 billion pesos, which it assigned at 26.22 percent.
Credit maturities for Friday were estimated at 7.464 billion pesos.
Dealers said secondary interest rates would tend to increase if upside pressure on long bond yields and peso weakness persisted.
